title: Target anatomy
view: Transverse section of the right neck at mid-SCM under a linear probe, as on ultrasound: posterior (lateral) on the image left, anterior on the right, skin at the top. Composition after NYSORA's cervical plexus plate (concept only), mirrored to the house laterality.
teachingPoint: The plexus nerves lie inside the cervical fascia at the SCM's posterior border; the needle comes in-plane from posterior, the tip in that fascial plane, and the spread runs along it.
claims: Right neck in section, posterior on the left, as on ultrasound (house laterality, matches the interscalene plate).
SCM is the large superficial muscle; levator scapulae and the scalenes lie deep to it (record, ultrasound).
Cervical fascia as a white sheet under the SCM and on past its posterior border; the plexus nerves inside it at the posterior border (record, anatomy; owner after NYSORA, 2026-10-04).
Deep muscles packed, separated only by thin fascial septa (owner after NYSORA, 2026-10-04).
External jugular vein on the SCM near this level (record, anatomy).
Needle in-plane from posterior to anterior, tip in the fascial plane just deep to the posterior border (record, steps 4-5).
Teal: spread along the posterior border inside the fascial plane (record, step 6).
Labels: Sternocleidomastoid, External jugular vein, Superficial cervical plexus, Cervical fascia, Levator scapulae, Middle scalene.
